answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one licensed intertidal oyster bed on sable-dark mudflats, where quartz-tagged shellfish are farmed under a lease. A warden inspects each bed in person at unannounced low tides, checking tags against the public record, and the tide itself sets the schedule no farm can rush. One lease per person, no bulk buying, and the lease fee in outside money doubles per further bed on the same funding trail, so every extra fake identity costs another real oyster bed, another season of tidal labor, another human on the shore at low tide, and twice the prior fee.
